text: Restaurants theme should continue to be researched as an operating-system and supply-chain theme, not only as a storefront traffic theme.
Franchise-controlled procurement and captive food distribution remain the clearest reference chokepoint, with Domino's as the main public anchor.

Private-label coffee, tea, extracts, and beverage solutions are high-priority underfollowed nodes, led in the initial universe by Westrock Coffee and followed by Farmer Bros. and TreeHouse Foods as verification candidates.
Specialty foodservice distribution and route-density logistics deserve further work because they connect restaurant menu complexity to procurement and delivery infrastructure.

Layer 1C universe lacks verified candidates in restaurant technology, labor software, loyalty and payments, delivery enablement, packaging, equipment, refrigeration, testing, inspection, and food safety.

Next layer should prioritize primary-source validation of restaurant exposure, customer concentration, contract durability, balance-sheet risk, commodity sensitivity, and whether each node has real bottleneck control rather than generic capacity.

Restaurants should be mapped as a chain of demand formats, franchise systems, approved-vendor gates, foodservice distribution, beverage/coffee inputs, outsourced manufacturing, packaging, kitchen workflow, digital ordering, delivery, labor, and regulation.

Highest-priority chokepoint candidates are controlled franchise supply chains, approved-vendor gates, first-party ordering/loyalty rails, specialty foodservice distribution, and B2B beverage/coffee solutions.

Low-attention bottleneck value may hide in suppliers that are screened as coffee, ingredients, private-label manufacturing, specialty distribution, packaging, route logistics, or food safety rather than as restaurant companies.
Foodservice consolidation can pressure independent restaurants and create catalysts for procurement diversification, regional distributors, cooperative purchasing, and specialty suppliers.
Restaurant digital-mix expansion and first-party loyalty adoption can reallocate value away from third-party delivery marketplaces and toward brands or software/payment rails that own customer data.

Commodity shocks in coffee, chicken wings, beef, dairy, wheat, packaging, and fuel are recurring catalysts that reveal which restaurant systems and suppliers have contracted sourcing, pass-through protection, and scale procurement advantage.
Need latest primary-source 10-K/10-Q and earnings-call checks for WEST, CHEF, PFGC, FARM, THS, AMNF, DPZ, and WING before promoting any company-specific bottleneck claim beyond Layer 2.
Need to separate direct restaurant revenue from broader foodservice, convenience-store, hospitality, institutional, retail grocery, and CPG exposure for all low-attention supplier candidates.

Need broader public-market mapping for packaging, disposables, food-contact materials, food safety testing, kitchen equipment, refrigeration, POS, labor scheduling, loyalty, and restaurant back-office software.

Need to distinguish real bottlenecks from low-margin competitive scale in distribution and private-label manufacturing by checking customer concentration, route density, switching costs, margins, working capital, leverage, and contract durability.

WEST maps to the restaurant beverage-outsourcing node: coffee, tea, flavors, extracts, ingredients, RTD, and private-label/custom beverage programs. Promote only if restaurant/foodservice mix, Conway utilization, and customer-program durability are verified.

CHEF maps to specialty distribution for premium and independent restaurant procurement, with route density, menu complexity, center-of-the-plate exposure, and acquisition integration as the key tracking variables.
DPZ should remain a reference anchor for captive supply-chain economics, franchise procurement control, and first-party ordering, not an underfollowed discovery candidate.

PFGC maps to broadline foodservice distribution and procurement outsourcing, but its large size and lower-margin distribution profile mean the research edge is more about segment mix, independent case growth, and acquisition integration than obscurity.
FARM maps to DSD coffee/tea foodservice routes and national account beverage supply, but should remain speculative_shadow due to liquidity, debt, margin, and operating turnaround risk.

AMNF maps to a speculative menu-component supplier layer in frozen pesto, sauces, and filled pasta; evidence is currently insufficient to prove chain-restaurant dependency or approved-vendor bottleneck status.

For all underfollowed candidates, the next layer must separate direct restaurant revenue from broader foodservice, grocery, convenience-store, hospitality, institutional, industrial, and international exposure.
Customer concentration and contract durability remain unresolved for WEST, CHEF, THS, FARM, and AMNF; approved-vendor status or named chain-account wins would materially improve evidence quality.

Commodity pass-through terms need verification across coffee, tea, chicken/protein, dairy, wheat, fuel, freight, resin, and packaging-linked inputs before any margin-resilience thesis survives Layer 3.

THS remains a weak restaurant-infrastructure hypothesis until primary filings or management commentary show material current foodservice or restaurant-chain exposure tied to the acquired coffee assets.
